stdout: (no config - demo: three prompts in a fictional PLG product; every count is an example input)
AAJ - UPGRADE PROMPT FUNNEL (last 30 days, 95% intervals)
ONE PROMPT TO FIX FIRST - "Export to PDF" at the click stage.
71 upgrades through prompts from 5000 active free users (1.4%).
Prompt                    Hit    Seen   Click  Paid  Seen -> paid (interval)
STAGES
Seat limit (3 users): delivery 90%  |  click 24.1%  |  checkout 30%  |  54.9% of upgrades
Export to PDF: delivery 97.8%  |  click 8%  |  checkout 20%  |  19.7% of upgrades
Project limit (5): delivery 62.5%  |  click 24%  |  checkout 30%  |  25.4% of upgrades
WHERE THE UPGRADES ARE (vs your best prompt's lower bound at each stage)
+22.4  Export to PDF - click (saw -> clicked): 8% vs 20.7% (Seat limit (3 users))
+9.8  Project limit (5) - delivery (hit limit -> saw prompt): 62.5% vs 96.6% (Export to PDF)
+2.9  Seat limit (3 users) - delivery (hit limit -> saw prompt): 90% vs 96.6% (Export to PDF)
+2.0  Export to PDF - checkout (clicked -> paid): 20% vs 22.8% (Seat limit (3 users))
PROMPT VS PROMPT (seen -> paid, Holm-corrected)
Seat limit (3 users) 7.2% vs Export to PDF 1.6%: p = 0.0000, adjusted 0.0000 -> different
Seat limit (3 users) 7.2% vs Project limit (5) 7.2%: p = 0.9910, adjusted 0.9910 -> not distinguishable
Export to PDF 1.6% vs Project limit (5) 7.2%: p = 0.0000, adjusted 0.0000 -> different
FINDINGS

!  Fix first: "Export to PDF" at click (saw -> clicked). It runs at 8%; "Seat limit (3 users)" runs at 24.1% at the same stage, and no lower than 20.7% at 95% confidence. Matching the lower figure would add about 22.4 upgrades per period. Prompts reach different users, so test the fix rather than assume it.
i  60 users hit "Seat limit (3 users)" without seeing the prompt. Check whether that is a deliberate frequency cap or a bug.
i  20 users hit "Export to PDF" without seeing the prompt. Check whether that is a deliberate frequency cap or a bug.
i  150 users hit "Project limit (5)" without seeing the prompt. Check whether that is a deliberate frequency cap or a bug.
i  At most 1900 of 5000 active free users hit a tracked limit (fewer if users hit several). The rest never met an upgrade moment; check whether the limits sit where value is proven.
